answer: To see what items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and view the Wix Stores reports. Use the Store Conversion Funnel (which tracks 'added to cart' as a conversion measure), Most Abandoned Products (shows products placed in a cart but not bought), Abandoned Carts Funnel, or Abandoned Carts Summary to analyze cart contents and abandonment. To see how items were sold, go to All Reports in your site's dashboard and view the Sales section reports, specifically Sales by item (breakdown of specific items and services sold), or in the Wix Stores section use Sales by Product Variant or Sales by Product Category.

To rename a web link (menu item) on your site: Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Choose Rename to change the name of the item on your site menu.

If your updated share image (og:image) is not appearing, first make sure you published your site after making the change. Then use the platform's inspection tool to force a refresh: for Facebook, go to the Facebook debugger, enter your site URL, click Debug, then click 'Scrape Again' (you may need to click it a few times) or 'Fetch new information' for URLs never shared before; for LinkedIn, log in and use the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/), enter the page URL, and the preview should show the correct image. Note that platforms may cache old data: Facebook may take some time to process new information, and LinkedIn can take up to a week for new information to appear in shares. Also ensure your og:image has an aspect ratio of 1.91:1 (width 1.9x the height) to avoid cropping issues.

In the New Automation Builder, when you edit your automated email template, you can add personalized content (also called dynamic values or variables) to insert the recipient's name. Go to Automations in your site's dashboard, create or edit an automation with 'Send an email' as the action, click the action to open the panel, then under 'Create an email' choose Edit and select 'Add personalized content to the email' to include dynamic values like the contact's first name.

According to the provided documentation, Wix Stores is designed for selling physical and digital products (including dropshipping items, subscriptions, and gift cards). The Wix Stores documentation does not list services as a sellable item type within the store. While the general Wix platform allows you to 'provide services and take bookings,' this is described as a separate capability from the Wix Stores online store product catalog.

Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content from your desktop Editor, and all Wix Editor templates are responsive on different screen sizes by default. If your site is not displaying correctly on mobile, you can adjust the layout by dragging elements in the mobile Editor or by using the Page Layout Optimizer tool (click Page Layout Optimizer on the left side of the mobile Editor, then click Optimize Now). Note: If you are using the latest Editor experience, the Page Layout Optimizer is not available because Wix automatically optimizes your mobile layout. Changing the layout on the mobile site does not affect the desktop site.

This issue typically occurs when the image scaling setting on your strip is set to 'Tile' (which causes the image to repeat/multiply across the space) or 'Original Size' (which can cause parts of the image to be cut off). To fix this: 1) Go to your editor and select the image on the strip. 2) If the image takes up the whole strip, click 'Change Strip Background'; if it's in a column only, click 'Change Column Background'. 3) Click 'Settings' and scroll down to 'Scaling & Positioning'. 4) Click the 'How's the image scaled?' drop-down and select 'Scale to Fill' (resizes to fill available space without cutting off or tiling). 5) You can also select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to choose which part of the image is in focus. Alternatively, you can crop the image to better fit the available space.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve this error: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact Wix support and provide details including the specific error with a screenshot, your Wix username/email, domain and site name, operating system, browsers tried, geographic location/ISP, security programs installed, and troubleshooting steps already attempted.

For gaps at the bottom of your page on the desktop version, you can try the following solutions: (1) If there is a gap between the page content and the footer, adjust the page height by clicking and dragging the Adjust Page Height icon, or change the page design by selecting a different preset design. Note: If your page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to access the main page area. (2) If there is a gap below the footer on your live site, you can: change the page background color to match the footer color, add more content to your page to cover the viewport, resize the footer to make it longer, or check the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap and delete or reposition them.

If you previously verified your site with Google manually (using the meta tag method in Google Search Console), your site is already connected. You don't need to complete the 'Connect site to Google' step in your SEO Setup Checklist. If that step is still marked as not completed in your checklist, you can ignore it.

To update inventory for many variants at once, use the bulk edit feature for product variants. Go to Store Products in your site's dashboard, select a product that has product options, and make sure the 'Manage pricing and inventory for variants' toggle is enabled. Click Edit, then select which variants to update: check the box at the top left to select all variants, use the 'All' drop-down to select variants with a specific option choice, or check individual variant checkboxes. From the options at the top right, choose Edit Inventory, enter the inventory amount, and click Apply. For advanced bulk edits across multiple products, go to the Inventory tab in your dashboard, select the products with checkboxes, click Update Inventory, and choose to Add or Set the same inventory level for all selected products.

Check that your dataset is set to 'Read' or 'Read & Write' mode. According to the documentation, your dataset needs to be in 'Read' or 'Read & Write' mode to read your collection items and apply sort conditions. If your dataset is set to 'Write' mode, it cannot read your collection content, so it cannot display the content or apply filters or sorts. Change the dataset mode in the dataset settings to 'Read' or 'Read & Write' to ensure your alphabetical sort conditions are applied on the published site.

Site visitors can check your calendar by viewing the Google Event Calendar app displayed on your site. You control what they see by going to the calendar in your Editor, clicking Settings, then the Calendars tab, where you select which calendars are visible to site visitors and which are visible but with details hidden (busy). Events marked as private will not show details unless you enable the 'Show private events' toggle in the Display tab. Visitors can then browse your calendar in the layout you chose (monthly, weekly, or agenda) directly on your website.

To add and format text in a Rich Text field in the CMS: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click the relevant collection, then click the Rich Text field for the relevant item. Enter the text you want to use and choose from the available formatting options at the top of the editor (e.g., Bold, Themes, Alignment, Link). You can click the Expand icon to edit the text in a larger window. The Rich Text editor uses the same font theme as your site, so updating your site's text theme in the Wix Editor or Studio Editor will adjust the heading and paragraph styles used in the Rich Text editor. Repeat these steps for each relevant collection item.

If recurring retries are enabled for the subscription's grace period, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from the customer's existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. Alternatively, the customer can manually resolve the failed payment by going to the My Subscriptions page in the Members Area, clicking Submit Payment next to the failed payment notification, and choosing their existing payment method to complete the payment.

The Company number (company registration number / business number / EIN / UTR / tax ID) you enter must exactly match your company's registered information. Re-enter the correct Company number and upload a company registration document that proves the validity and ownership of that specific number (Tax ID / EIN / Registration Number). Also confirm that the Legal Business Name and the Company number entered match those associated with your business bank account.

To resize an image in your section: Click the image, then drag the handles on the edges of the image to the size you want (using the corner handles keeps the original proportions). To add text to your new section: Click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click a category, and drag the element onto the section.

According to the documentation, menu item text should update automatically: if you rename a page in the Pages & Menu panel, it automatically updates on your site menu, and if you rename the item on your site menu, it automatically updates the Pages & Menu panel. The retrieved documentation does not provide specific troubleshooting steps for when menu item text fails to update or appears glitched.

The provided documentation does not specify the exact cost of 1 Business Starter Google Workspace email. It only states that business email prices depend on the Google Workspace plan chosen and that Business Starter is one of three available plans (along with Business Standard and Business Plus).

The provided Wix Stores documentation does not describe a specific feature or label for marking an item as 'low in stock.' The documented inventory management methods are: (1) Tracking inventory, where you enter a numeric quantity in the Inventory field (which updates automatically when sales are made), or (2) manually assigning an 'In Stock' or 'Out of Stock' status. To update a specific shoe item, go to the Inventory tab in your site's dashboard (or use the Wix app), locate the product, and either enter a low number in the Inventory field or select the appropriate stock status from the drop-down.

The provided documentation does not contain specific information about whether a paid ad will appear in the campaign list after being reviewed, nor does it specify whether campaign payments are automatically deducted from a credit card or require manual credit top-ups.

The search results describe enabling 'Shipping & delivery rates' on the Cart Page and setting up local delivery areas in Wix Stores settings, but do not explain how to display delivery information directly on the Product Page itself.

The documentation states that Wix Email Marketing can be used for free, with the number of emails you can send depending on your monthly balance (visible in your email marketing dashboard). To send more emails per month, you must upgrade your email marketing plan. However, the specific pricing amounts or tiers for the paid email marketing plans are not detailed in the provided documentation.

For images carried over from desktop, it only states that you can adjust image settings (Reset Image Proportions and Image Behaviors), crop the image, or add an animation.

The documentation does not list the exact event names or configuration steps specific to Wix Bookings services.

While the articles describe how to change providers generally (via Accept Payments in the dashboard), disconnect providers, or process refunds, none address any restrictions or special procedures that apply when funds have already been sent for an order.

It states that business email prices depend on factors including the Google Workspace plan you choose (Business Starter, Business Standard, or Business Plus), and that you should compare plans based on the number of emails you plan to send and features needed, but no specific dollar amounts are listed.

The available docs cover general automation conditions (text, number, date/time operators), Wix Bookings triggers (such as 'Session booked', 'Client checked in', etc.), and customizing automated emails, but none mention a birthday trigger or how to configure birthday-based automations to send a free class offer.

It can take time for Google to recognize that old URLs have changed or are no longer available, as the removal process depends entirely on the individual search engines and requires them to recrawl your site. Since you have already submitted removal requests and your updated sitemap, ensure your site is verified with Google Search Console, then after sending each removal request, ask Google to crawl the page again by requesting indexing for it. This prompts Google to recrawl and update its index. Note that even after these steps, it can still take some time for Google to fully remove the pages from search results.

Documents may be rejected for several specific reasons. For your photo ID: it must be a color, active/non-expired passport, driver's license, or government ID showing all 4 borders and corners, not blurry/overexposed/copied (e.g., screenshot), straightened (not angled/rotated), with no information blocked or blacked out. Your first, middle, and last name and birth date in your Wix Payments account must exactly match the ID. For passports with a Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ), the MRZ must be visible; for driver's licenses or government ID cards, send a separate file for each side. For address verification (e.g., utility bill): must be visible/clear, dated within the last 6 months, and complete (full page minimum with full name and address visible). For bank documents (bank statement, voided check, or bank letter): must be a color copy with the bank logo visible, full bank account number visible, issued within the last 12 months, and the account holder/company name must match the Wix Payments account owner (personal) or the legal business name in your dashboard (business). Banking documents are rejected if blurry, illegible, torn/damaged, rotated/upside down, a mobile screenshot, missing full account numbers, name/company mismatch, incorrect account numbers, a direct deposit form instead of a bank statement, or a voided check not printed by a financial institution. For company documents: tax ID/registration number and company name must be visible/clear and match your Wix Payments account, issued within the last 12 months. All documents must be issued within the same country as your selected business location (for business accounts, your ID may be from any Wix Payments supported country). Files must be HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, or PNG, max 10 MB, min 1 KB for PDF / 100 KB for other formats. If 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed all details match, contact Wix Customer Care.

Wix Payments is currently only available in specific countries and currencies: Austria (EUR), Belgium (EUR), Brazil (BRL), Canada (CAD), Finland (EUR), Germany (EUR), Ireland (EUR), Italy (EUR), Lithuania (EUR), Netherlands (EUR), Portugal (EUR), Spain (EUR), Switzerland (CHF), United Kingdom (GBP), and United States (USD). If you see a region error, check your business location at the top right of the Accept Payments dashboard and change it if incorrect; if Wix Payments is not available in your region, you will see locally available payment providers instead. For currency errors, the currency in your Wix account must match the currency in your payment provider account. To change your site currency, go to Settings in your site's dashboard, click Language & Region, scroll to Currency, select your currency from the drop-down menu, and click Save.

To add a subscribe form to your site in the Wix Editor: Go to your editor, click Add Elements on the left side, then click Contact & Forms. Scroll down to the Subscribe section and drag a form onto your site. Click Settings to customize layout, design, and manage submissions. Alternatively, if you're using Wix ADI: Click Add on the top bar, select Section to Page, click Subscribe, and choose a layout. You can also add a subscribe form to your site's footer by clicking the footer in the ADI builder and selecting the checkbox next to Subscribe. Once added, visitors who fill out the form are automatically added to your contact list with a 'Subscriber' label.

To update the terms & conditions checkbox at checkout in Wix Stores, go to Checkout settings in your site's dashboard, click Policies, select the checkbox next to the policy you want to display, and enter the policy text. To make the agreement checkbox appear, click the Policy agreement checkbox toggle to enable it. Optionally, select the Checked by default checkbox if you want the agreement checked by default.

If you followed the steps to change the browser tab title (Editor > Pages & Menu/Pages > More Actions > SEO basics > Title tag > Publish) but it's still not working, check if you have added any custom code to your site. Custom code can affect your browser tab title and override the title tag setting. Try removing any custom code you added to your site to see if the correct browser tab title appears. Also note that search engines will update your page's title tag the next time they crawl your site, but the live site browser tab should update immediately after publishing.

Since you have a Google Workspace Admin account, you can reset the password for your second business Gmail account as an admin. To reset a user's password: 1) Sign in to your Google Admin account. 2) Click Password, then Reset Password. 3) Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a password. (Note: By default, password minimum length is 8 characters.) 4) (Optional) To view the password, click Preview. 5) (Optional) To require the user to change the password at next sign-in, enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle. 6) Click Reset. 7) (Optional) To paste the password somewhere, such as in a Google Chat conversation with the user, click 'Click to copy password'. 8) Choose to email the password to the user, or click Done.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with your Wix site, first create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant (Admin > GA4 Setup Assistant > Get Started > Create property). Then copy your GA4 measurement ID from the Web stream details. On your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, click the Show More icon in the top right corner, then click Edit. Paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up (ensure no extra spaces), optionally select IP Anonymization, and click Save. If you are upgrading from Universal Analytics, note that UA properties stopped collecting data on July 1, 2023, and you can use both properties simultaneously by connecting your UA tracking ID to your GA4 property in Google Analytics Admin settings.

Your payments go to your Wix Payments account first, then are transferred (paid out) to your bank account. Each payment goes through 3 stages: processing (2-5 business days), scheduled payout (added to your next daily, weekly, or monthly payout based on your settings), and sent payout (funds sent to your bank account, arriving within 3-5 business days). You can view payout details including Payout ID and Payout Date in your payments table or Payouts section of your dashboard.

For a page without a footer, click on the page itself (not a footer), then click and drag the Adjust Page Height handle located at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note: This option is only available if you have selected the 'No Header & Footer' layout for that page. If the handle isn't moving, an element may be blocking the resize—you cannot make the page shorter if doing so would cut off an element at the bottom. Move or delete the blocking element first; if you can't find it, use the Layers panel to locate it. You can also double-click the handle to reset the height.

To set up a table and connect it to your collection in Wix Studio: 1) First create a multiple-item collection in CMS (go to CMS in your dashboard or editor, click Create Collection, name it, leave 'Multiple items' selected, add fields manually or import CSV, and set permissions). 2) Add a table to your page: click Add Elements on the left, click Layout Tools, click Tables, then drag your chosen table design onto the page. 3) Connect the table to your collection: click the table element, click the Connect to CMS icon, then in the Inspector panel choose the dataset you want to display (select an existing dataset or add a new one and choose your collection). Supported collection fields automatically appear as columns. 4) Set up columns via Manage Table: reorder columns by dragging, change column names via Edit label, delete columns, or manage connections to change which fields connect to each column. 5) Customize further using the Settings icon (clicking behavior, link opening, date format), the Design tab in the Inspector (colors, borders, text), and the Layout icon (table height, column width, header display, alignment).

It is not possible to edit or modify a domain once purchased. When you register a domain name you reserve the letters or characters in that order. If you have already made the purchase, the only way to change the domain name is to register a new domain. Important: Domains purchased through Wix are set to renew automatically. We recommend that you turn the auto renewal option off for the incorrect domain to avoid paying for another year.

According to the documentation, it is not possible to restore deleted Wix Stores products. Site History cannot restore certain page types such as Wix Stores products, and CMS backups do not affect Wix App collections (including Wix Stores) because they get their content from the relevant app.

To sync an external calendar (iCal) with Wix Hotels so visitors can only book available dates, import your iCal URL into Wix Hotels: 1) Locate your iCal URL from your external calendar service. 2) Go to your Wix dashboard, click the Hotels tab, expand the Reservations tab, and select iCal. 3) Click the Choose Type drop-down menu and select a room type. 4) Paste your iCal URL into the URL field. 5) (Optional) Click Add Calendar to add another room type and paste its iCal URL. 6) Click Save. Important: The sync is one-way only (from the external iCal to your Wix Calendar), so imported reservations will block those dates on your site. If you have multiple room types, you must add a different iCal URL for each room type. Note: This feature is not compatible with the Wix Hotels Channel Manager—if you want to use the Channel Manager, delete all URLs in this tab first.

To transfer an edited page from your duplicated (copy) site back to your original site, use the copy and paste feature between sites in the Wix Editor: 1) Open the Editor of the copy site containing the edited page. 2) Click Menus & Pages (or Pages & Menu) on the left side of the Editor. 3) Right-click the relevant page and click Copy. 4) Open the Editor of your original site (the target site). 5) Right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or select Paste & Apply Site Theme to apply the original site's color and text themes). 6) Rename the new page if needed by entering the new name and clicking Done. Note: The pasted page is always added as a main page to the target site's menu, even if it was a subpage in the copy. You cannot copy anchors, links, folders, lightboxes, router pages, or pages from third-party/Wix business solution apps.

To set one og:image for your entire site: open your site's settings in the dashboard, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image, click Upload Image, select or upload your image, click Choose File, then click Save at the top of the dashboard and publish your site. Regarding where the image appears: the documentation states that open graph (og) tags are used by social networks to display images when a page is shared, and explicitly lists Instagram (along with Facebook, X/Twitter, and LinkedIn) as platforms that use your Social Share settings. The retrieved documentation does not mention email clients, so it does not specify whether the og:image will affect previews when the link is sent via email.

To transfer the edited page from your duplicate (copy) site to the original site without overwriting the original page: In the duplicate site's Editor, click Menus & Pages on the left, right-click the edited page and select Copy. Then open the Editor of your original site, right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or press Ctrl+V / Cmd+V). The pasted page is added as a new main page in the Site Menu page list, so the original page is not overwritten. You can then rename the new page (enter the new name and click Done) to distinguish it from the original.

To download your website visit reports for December 15 to January 15: Go to All Reports in your site's dashboard (under Analytics), select the relevant traffic report (such as Traffic over time), ensure the report view is customized to your desired date range, click the Download drop-down at the top right, and select a file format (Excel, CSV, or Image). Reports can be downloaded including their customized view.

To cancel within the 14-day money-back period: Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account, click the More Actions icon next to the relevant plan, click Cancel Plan, then click Cancel Now to confirm. If you cancel within the first 14 days, your plan ends immediately and you receive a full refund (allow up to 20 business days for it to appear on your statement).

Wix offers 800+ pre-set website templates created by Wix designers. These templates include sample content, color themes, galleries, inner pages, and built-in business features. They are organized into categories based on business intent and are fully customizable—you can add, rearrange, and remove content and apps to match your needs. Templates are available for the Wix Editor, Editor X, and Studio Editor. You can also start from a blank canvas or a wireframe template if you prefer. Additionally, you can save pre-made designs from any Wix template to 'My Designs' to reuse them across other sites in your account.

To move your domain from one site to another in your Wix account: Go to Domains in your Wix account and scroll to the domain you want to reassign. Click the Domain Actions icon on the right and select 'Assign to a Different Site'. Select the site you want to connect the domain to and click Next. If that site is currently connected to a different domain, choose either 'Redirect it to the primary domain' (to redirect your domain to the site's existing primary domain) or 'Replace the current primary domain' (to connect your domain and disconnect the site's current domain), then click Assign.

According to the Wix documentation, you can use the third-party app "Blocky: IP & Country Blocker by Effective Apps" to block visitors from certain countries from accessing your site. The app allows you to block visitors from specific countries, block specific IP addresses, and immediately block multiple countries with a click of a button. After a visitor is blocked, they are automatically redirected to a page of your choice on your site. To get started, check out the Blocky: IP & Country Blocker app in the Wix App Market. For questions or support, contact Effective Apps directly at support@effectify.co or visit https://effectify.co/.

For assistance with all questions on generating and accessing authorization codes, go to: http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/analytics/spss/licensing/Auth_Codes_092910_2.html. You may also visit the Predictive Analytics Community Get Help page at https://developer.ibm.com/predictiveanalytics/get-help/ for direct links to the License Key Center and information about your Support options.

The segmentation fault (GPF) occurs because the installed GTK libraries are not at the specific required versions for IBM Installation Manager on AIX. While the libraries are present, the Technote explicitly states that a segmentation error occurs when the gtk libraries are installed but are not at the required versions. You must ensure the exact required versions of the GTK libraries listed in the IBM Required gtk libraries for IBM Installation Manager on AIX Technote are installed, rather than simply having the latest available versions.

The Linux KVM monitoring agent is not listed among the agents verified to run properly with CANDLEDATA. The documentation states that only agents LO, LZ, UD, and UX have been verified to work with CANDLEDATA, and explicitly notes that not all agents have been verified. To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) on 64-bit JVMs, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. This removes the use of compressed references and therefore removes the lower 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, allowing native memory to grow beyond 4GB. Note that this will result in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so the Java heap size should be adjusted to a larger value and garbage collection monitored and retuned as required. Before using -Xnocompressedrefs, rule out the possibility of a native memory leak, since native memory will grow unbounded.

The network connection for the data source may become invalid after a period of inactivity. A typical cause is that a firewall between the Application Server and the Database has a policy to discard network connections that remain idle for some time, causing the pooled connection to become stale and resulting in connection failures when the application attempts to use it after a day or two.

IBM Security Bulletin swg21985013 addresses CVE-2016-0394: IBM Integration Bus (IIB) V9 and WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) V8, upon installation on Unix platforms, set incorrect permissions for an object (the isadc directory), which could allow a local attacker to manipulate certain files. CVSS Base Score is 4.0 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N). Remediation is available via APAR IT14845 in IBM Integration Bus Fix Pack 9.0.0.6 and WebSphere Message Broker Fix Pack 8.0.0.8. For current installations on Unix, a workaround is to run: find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \; ; find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \; ; find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -name *.sh -print -exec chmod 755. For unsupported versions, upgrade to a fixed, supported version.
The Sybase Server Agent 620 FP2 installer (6.2.0-TIV-ITM_SYB-FP0002) can be downloaded from IBM Passport Advantage using part number CNN25ML.

The Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries required to initialize SSL (HTTPS), causing the HTTPS transport to be skipped. To resolve this, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory that ships with the Plug-in. For a 64-bit Plug-in v8.x (such as 8.5) on a 64-bit system, use: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/ (adjust the path for 32-bit or other bit-depth combinations as needed). On Linux, setting this variable from the command line before starting the web server may not work; instead, add the export command to /etc/sysconfig/httpd for RHEL or /usr/sbin/envvars for SLES/SUSE so the variable is set when the web server starts.

To resolve the 'MBeanStarter loadExtensions failed to load extension' error at Portal startup without installing a fix, use the local fix from APAR PI34677: 1) Open the WAS admin console. 2) Navigate to Resources > Resource environment providers > WP ScriptingService > Custom properties. 3) Locate the entry with name 'ServerExt.applications' and value 'com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions'. 4) Delete this entry, save the changes, and restart the Portal server.

You can find the required authorizations by looking at the /IBMMON/AUTH profile available in the ITM transport imported into your SAP system. By default, the MySAP agent uses the userid IBMMON_AGENT created together with the /IBMMON/AUTH role and profile. If you create your own userid instead, you must provide it with the same set of minimum required authorization settings defined for the /IBMMON/AUTH profile to ensure successful data collection. Depending on the transport level, the required authorization may vary, but you can always refer to the values specified for the /IBMMON/AUTH profile in the transport.

The 3-second WLM wait ('WaitForWLMDat ... Sleeping for 2999 ms') is controlled by the sib.trm.linger property, which sets the messaging engine lookup delay that the Work Load Manager/HA manager uses before returning. Tune the sib.trm.linger value in the sib.properties file: place it under <WAS_HOME>/properties (applies to all profiles) or <PROFILE_ROOT>/properties (applies to all servers in that profile; the profile-level value takes precedence if defined in both). The technote notes the default linger is three seconds and that if the HA manager cannot locate the running messaging engine within three seconds (e.g., under heavy load) you should consider increasing sib.trm.linger from three to give the HA manager more time; adjust this value to address the remote-queue delay and then restart the server after changing the property.
The transaction log gets corrupted when the IBM Content Collector server runs out of disk space, causing the Configuration Store Service to become hung and unresponsive to start/stop commands.

In a clustered environment, the most common cause for the latest ruleset not executing after a 'Replace RuleApp Version' deployment is that the hot deployment notification was not successfully sent or received by all Execution Units (XU). Specifically: (1) The user publishing the ruleset update must have sufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) for the deployment to notify all Execution Units through JMX; without this, the cluster nodes may not receive the update notification. (2) The updated ruleset may have failed to parse successfully, causing RES to fall back on an earlier active version that parses. (3) If asynchronous ruleset parsing is enabled, an earlier version may be used while the updated ruleset is being parsed. (4) Verify that the ruleset path requested does not specify a version, as a path without a version requests the highest version, whereas a version-specific path would execute that specific version. Ensure the RES components (Execution Unit, Management Console, and client) are properly installed and that hot deployment notifications are reaching all cluster nodes.

The clearing event is being dropped because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after receiving the event, so it never appears in the EIF logs or OMNIbus. To resolve this, set the connection_mode in om_tec.config on the ITM Server (TEMS) to connection_less instead of connection oriented by changing 'ConnectionMode=co' to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

The error occurs because the Windows security policy 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' is enabled, which prevents the FIPS key from being encrypted during import. To resolve this: 1) Open Local Security Policy under Administrative Tools, 2) Navigate to Local Policies > Security Options, 3) Set 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' to Disabled, then retry the key import.

IBM Integration Bus Hypervisor Edition V9.0 and WebSphere Message Broker Hypervisor Edition V8.0 ship with Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Server 6.2, which is vulnerable to CVE-2017-14746, CVE-2017-15085, CVE-2017-15086, CVE-2017-15087, and CVE-2017-15275. Remediation: IBM strongly recommends contacting Red Hat to obtain and install fixes for RHEL Server 6.2, as applicable.

Yes. IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance supports SHA-2 (SHA-256). Specifically, when a Certificate Authority (CA) signs a certificate using SHA2 (SHA-256), DataPower can validate the CA's signature on the certificate while building the trust chain from the DataPower ValCred. SHA-2 algorithms (such as hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-512, and diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256) are also supported in SSH configurations.

The error IQQG0205E indicates that the version of the IBM FileNet Content Search Services client files embedded in the IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine is not compatible with the IBM FileNet Content Search Services server version. The client supports specific server versions and the server supports specific client versions, and these do not match in your environment. To resolve this, ensure that the version of the IBM FileNet Content Search Services client files included in the Content Platform Engine matches the version of the Content Search Services server. Check the readme files for your installed Content Platform Engine and Content Search Services fix packs, as they include the required fix pack compatibility requirements (for example, IBM Content Search Services 5.2.1.5 requires specific Content Platform Engine fix packs such as 5.2.1.5-P8CPE-FP005).

In the db2diag.log corruption entry, locate the line containing Obj={pool:<tablespace_id>;obj:<object_id>;type:<type>}. The fields map as follows: pool = Tablespace ID, obj = Object ID, and type = object type (0 = Table, 1 = Index). To find the object name, run: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>". For example, for Obj={pool:3;obj:21;type:0}, run: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=21 and tbspaceid=3".

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, the Class Pointer and Monitor/Lock fields in Java objects are stored as 32-bit values, so they must be allocated in native memory within the first 4GB of the address space (the low-memory region under 4GB). Even if the Java heap is placed above 4GB and the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust the low-memory region first. When the JVM later tries to allocate a Class Pointer or Monitor/Lock that must reside in that lower 4GB, the allocation fails and a Native OutOfMemory (NOOM) is thrown. The same can happen if the Java heap itself is small and allocated in the lower 4GB along with these structures. Additionally, on Linux/AIX an insufficient ulimit (nproc / thread limit) can cause a NOOM with 'Failed to create a thread' in the javacore. To address the low-memory shortage, options include -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address>, -Xmx4G, or (starting Java 6.0.16.3, 6.1.8.3, 7.0.8.10, 7.1.2.10) -Xmcrs to reserve more low-memory space at startup; if NOOM persists after these, investigate reducing application Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks usage and WebSphere native memory footprint.

When multiple JDBC driver jars from the same vendor (e.g., ojdbc6.jar and ojdbc14.jar) are present in the environment—whether configured in different scopes (cell/node/server) or referenced by WebSphere variables such as ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH—WebSphere Application Server cannot predict which driver class will be loaded first due to classloader collision. This causes the SystemOut.log to report the version of the older driver (ojdbc14.jar) even though the JDBC provider is configured for ojdbc6.jar. To resolve this, go to the JDBC Provider in the administrative console and enable "Isolate this resource provider". When enabled, it ensures that only the jar specified in that provider's classpath is used for all datasources under that provider, preventing the older driver from being loaded. Also verify that WebSphere variables (stored in variables.xml at cell and node scopes) do not reference the older jar.

The behavior is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the session timeout. In the TeamServer (RTS/DC) web module deployment descriptor (WEB-INF/web.xml), the context-param ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout is set to 600 seconds (10 minutes) by default. If a transactional operation performed by RTS/DC takes longer than this timeout to complete, the transaction is rolled back and the operation is not completed, which can appear as the user being kicked out while actively authoring rules. You can increase this value in the web.xml file of the RTS/DC EAR (jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear\teamserver.war\WEB-INF). Additionally, check application-server-level transaction timeouts (for example, on WebSphere Application Server the "Maximum transaction timeout"), since container-level transaction timeouts can also roll back long-running operations.

This error occurs because the Centera SDK library path (FPLibrary) was not loaded into java.library.path. According to the technote, changes made to the setCenteraLibPath.sh or setCenteraLibPath.bat file were not picked up by the WebSphere Application Server startup script (for example, if the Content Engine instance was restarted from within the WAS console rather than from the command line, or the setCenteraLibPath file was added to setupcmdLine.sh but not recognized). To resolve, after making any changes to the setCenteraLibPath.sh or setCenteraLibPath.bat file, restart WebSphere so the changes are detected and the CenteraSDK path is loaded.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg22004378 (titled 'IBM Security Bulletin: IBM MQ is affected by a potential denial of service to channel processes (CVE-2017-1557)'). The bulletin states that an IBM MQ application with authority to connect to a remote queue manager could send a malicious request causing undefined behavior within the channel process, including loss of service for other connections. CVE-2017-1557 has a CVSS Base Score of 4.3 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L). Affected versions include IBM MQ and IBM MQ Appliance v8.0.0.0 to v8.0.0.7, IBM MQ v9.0.0.0 LTS to v9.0.0.1 LTS, and IBM MQ/IBM MQ Appliance v9.0.1 CD to v9.0.3 CD. Remediation requires applying fix pack 8.0.0.8, 9.0.0.2, or upgrading to IBM MQ 9.0.4 respectively. No workarounds are available.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg22003510. CVE-2017-1236 describes a vulnerability where IBM MQ could allow an authenticated user to potentially cause a denial of service by issuing an incorrect saved channel status inquiry. CVSS Base Score is 3.1 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L). Affected products include IBM MQ 9.0.2 Continuous Delivery, IBM MQ Appliance 9.0.x Continuous Delivery, IBM MQ 9.0 LTS, IBM MQ 8.0, and IBM MQ 8.0 Appliance. Remediation involves applying IBM MQ 9.0.3 CD or later, continuous delivery update 9.0.3 or later for Appliance, Fix Pack 9.0.0.2 for 9.0 LTS, or Fix Pack 8.0.0.7 for 8.0. Workarounds include restarting the failed command server on the queue manager (or restarting the affected queue manager for IBM MQ Appliance).

To identify indexing errors in the Atlas database:

1. Login to the Atlas database as the PSSAPL user.
2. Run the query: select * from ctx_user_index_errors;
3. Copy the value in the ERR_TEXTKEY field from the results.
4. Run the query: select * from documentlibrary where rowid='<value from Step 3>';
5. This will list the document that has the indexing error.

Note: Sometimes encrypted and password protected documents cause document indexing errors.

This is a known DB2 defect documented in APAR PI19804. SQLCODE -401 (DSNT408I) with SQLERRP=DSNXOBFC occurs when creating a native SQL procedure (such as CIUSNTSR) that contains a control statement with an IN-LIST predicate referencing SQL variables (e.g., IF variable IN (sqlvar1, sqlvar2)). DB2 11 does not process the SQL variables in the IN-LIST predicate properly during CREATE PROCEDURE, resulting in the 'operands not comparable' error. Apply the PTF for APAR PI19804 (UI20622 for DB2 10; select the appropriate PTF for your DB2 11 component level) to resolve the issue.

This occurs because JARs in the WAS server's plugins directory enforce an 'exports list' via the server's class loader. Classes in plugin JARs that are not on this exports list are considered internal use only and cannot be called by user code, even though RAD's editor/compiler can see them. To resolve: either place the JAR in the server's library directory (where a different class loader is used that does not implement the exports list), or download the required class directly (e.g., from Apache) and place that JAR in the server's classpath instead of relying on the plugin JAR.

According to the supported operating system matrix, Apple Macintosh OS X Mavericks (10.9) only supports IBM SPSS Statistics 23 and IBM SPSS Statistics 22. The IBM SPSS Statistics Subscription Installer is not supported on OS X 10.9.5 because newer releases require later Mac OS versions (for example, OS X 10.10 Yosemite supports Statistics 22, 23, and 24; OS X 10.11 supports Statistics 24; OS X 10.12 supports Statistics 24 and 25; OS X 10.13 supports Statistics 25). To install the Subscription version, you must upgrade your Mac OS to a supported version, or use IBM SPSS Statistics 22 or 23 on OS X 10.9.5 (note that Statistics 22 on OS X 10.9 requires Apple Java SE 6 (1.6.0_65) to be installed first).

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg22012983 (CVE-2018-1371). An IBM MQ client connecting to an MQ queue manager can cause a SIGSEGV in the queue manager's amqrmppa channel process, terminating it. CVSS Base Score is 6.5 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). Affected versions include IBM MQ V8.0 (maintenance level 8.0.0.8), IBM MQ V9 LTS (9.0.0.0 - 9.0.0.2), and IBM MQ V9 CD (9.0.0 - 9.0.4). Remediation: apply FixPack 8.0.0.9 for V8.0, FixPack 9.0.0.3 for V9 LTS, or upgrade to 9.0.5 for V9 CD. Additional details are in swg22012992.

The error is caused by a corrupt installation of the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API. To resolve this, re-install the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API by: 1) Copying the software to a local disk, 2) Starting the re-installation of the .NET API, and 3) Selecting all sub-components of .NET Framework 4.5 that were not listed before (select them all if unsure). During the next installation of ICC there will be no further errors regarding missing components.

The available context covers IBM Content Navigator case sensitivity (which notes ICN metadata searches are case sensitive by default and that the 'Force Case Insensitive Search' flag applies to FileNet P8 object stores, not Workplace My Inbox), but nothing confirms whether the My Inbox where-filter can be made case insensitive or that 'Force case-insensitive search' affects it. Theme files are served from the browser or proxy cache (HTTP 304) because the resolver uses a digest to cache URLs, and this digest remains the same between restarts. To force the browser to load updated theme resources, set the 'digest.seed' key in the WP ConfigService to any string value. This generates a new digest on server boot, creating different URLs so the updated resources are loaded from the server instead of the cache.

For IIB v10.0.0.9 and later, use the mqsichangeproperties command to generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against a specific execution group (Integration Server):

mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core

Replace <Int.Node> with your integration node name and <Int.Server> with the target execution group name. The -v core option produces a javacore (thread dump) on IBM JRE platforms (all platforms except HP and Solaris). The dump file is output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors.

Note: Collection of Java core dumps is invasive and will impact the performance of the Integration Server process.
